Latin word

prōferō

prōferō, prōferre, prōtulī, prōlātum

verb

defer, adjourn; extend, enlarge (bounds); put off (a date); bring out, produce; to bring forward, quote, cite; utter, pronounce

In this lexicon

  • adjourn

    also used · classical · Cic. Att. 13.14.1: auctiōnis diem laxius prōferre (Lewis & Short s.v. prōferō)

  • extend

    also used · classical · Caes. BC 1.81 (Lewis & Short); Cic. Att. 13.14.1: auctiōnis diem laxius prōferre (Lewis & Short)

  • produce

    the recommended word · classical · Plaut. Am. 769: Vīn' prōferrī pateram? — Prōferrī volō.; Cic. Rosc. Com. 29: ex arcā (Lewis & Short)

  • quote

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. N.D. 1.113: librōs (Lewis & Short); Cic. de Orat. 2.290: auctōrēs (Lewis & Short)

  • utter

    also used · classical · Quint. 11.3.33: extrēmās syllabās (Lewis & Short); Traupman 401

  • at ille prōfert ipsum porcellum ē sinū

    but he produces the piglet itself from under his cloakPhaedr. 5.5.37
